justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Tendinopathy and scar tissue outcomes modest; not clearly superior to other soft tissue techniques.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: 2-day training course; moderate cost; requires ASTYM tool purchase; moderately accessible.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to soft tissue and musculoskeletal caseloads; useful in outpatient ortho and sports settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Billed under manual therapy CPT codes; standard commercial and Medicare coverage at manual therapy rates.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate employer demand as IASTM approach; valued in orthopedic PT practices using soft tissue techniques.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Some patients respond well; discomfort during treatment is a barrier.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Some cash-pay opportunity for tendinopathy/soft-tissue niches but largely insurance-billed.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Brand exists but competes with IASTM/Graston and is not strongly premium.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Crowded soft-tissue tool space; modest differentiation only.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Protocolized and trainable across staff with licensing fees.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Limited consumer recognition; clinicians know it more than patients.
justifications.business.efficiency: Course + per-clinician licensing fees add up; moderate ROI.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Commercial brand cert with negligible academic credibility.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Small handful of company-affiliated studies; limited independent literature.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Rarely part of core curriculum; may appear in modalities electives.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Evidence base is thin and largely industry-funded.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Time and licensing costs are not academically rewarded.
